events.detail: Jonathan Davis seen at Oakridge Family Medicine for left shoulder pain after a low-speed motorcycle fall, diagnosed with left AC joint sprain (Grade I/II) and mild rotator cuff tendinitis.
X-rays of left shoulder showed mild AC joint gapping with no fracture.
Physical therapy referred to Hope Valley for 12 sessions for left shoulder AC joint sprain.

EMS (Liberty County EMS Rescue 14) dispatched at 12:45 to NSK plant for industrial machinery entrapment; found Jonathan Davis, 28, with left arm crushed by metal stamping press, tourniquet applied by factory responder, IV Fentanyl 100mcg given, transported to Midwest Regional trauma unit.

Jonathan Davis admitted emergently to Midwest Regional Medical Center ICU-04 at 13:25 with admitting diagnosis of complete traumatic amputation between shoulder and elbow, left arm (S48.112A); attending Dr. Marcus Vance, admitting Dr. David Cho.
ED triage at 13:28, ESI Level 1 (Emergent), chief complaint left upper extremity entrapment/crush/near-amputation; BP 88/50, HR 130, RR 24, SpO2 93%, pain 10/10.
Emergency physician diagnostic impression: mangled unsalvageable left upper extremity with complete vascular and neurologic disruption, and traumatic shock secondary to acute blood loss and pain.

X-ray and CT angiography of left upper extremity showed extensive comminuted open segmental fractures of forearm/hand, comminuted displaced supracondylar humerus fracture, and complete cessation of contrast enhancement in the brachial artery at distal third humerus, consistent with unsalvageable limb.
Emergency blood transfusion initiated with 2 units PRBC prior to transfer to OR.

Emergent left transhumeral (above-elbow) amputation performed by Dr. Marcus Vance with myofascial closure, bone beveling, and traction-neurectomy of median, ulnar, and radial nerves; EBL 650 mL, JP drain placed.
Labs showed leukocytosis (WBC 14.2), anemia (Hgb 8.9, Hct 27.2), and urine drug screen positive for trace cannabinoids, negative ethanol.
Postoperative inpatient pain regimen initiated: Hydromorphone (Dilaudid) PCA, Gabapentin 300mg PO, Ancef (Cefazolin) 1g IV, and PRN Oxycodone 5-10mg PO.
ICU/trauma ward nursing monitoring showed improving vitals (BP 154/88 down to 131/87, HR 98 down to 82) and pain trending from 10 to 5 over 24 hours.
JP drain removed on postoperative day 4 per hospital course.

Discharged from Midwest Regional Medical Center after 7-day admission; transitioned to oral Oxycodone and Gabapentin 300mg TID, follow-up with Dr. Vance in 1 week and PM&R/prosthetic evaluation with Dr. Elena Rostova in 4 weeks.
Discharge medications: Gabapentin 300mg PO TID, Oxycodone 5mg PO q4-6h PRN, Cefdinir 300mg PO BID for 5 more days.
1-month orthopedic follow-up with Dr. Marcus Vance; stump fully healed but severe phantom limb pain (8/10) and stump hypersensitivity noted, especially over medial/posterior terminal stump.
Gabapentin increased to 600mg PO TID for phantom limb pain.
Referral made to Hope Valley for stump desensitization therapy and to NextStep Prosthetics (CPO Robert Chen) for initial shrinker sock fitting.

5-month orthopedic visit with Dr. Vance; new tender 1.5cm mobile nodule at distal medial left stump reproducing electrical shock pain, diagnosed as post-amputation traumatic neuroma of ulnar/median nerve stump interfering with prosthetic fitting.
Surgery scheduled for neuroma excision and deep muscle transposition, planned for 11/12/2024 to allow tissue maturation.
Left residual limb stump revision: excision of 1.8 x 1.4 cm neuroma of median/ulnar nerves with proximal nerve transposition and embedding into triceps muscle, performed by Dr. Marcus Vance.

Hope Valley notified attorney Marcus Vance Sr. that Liberty Mutual placed prosthetic therapy authorization on hold pending peer review of proposed Myoelectric Transhumeral Prosthesis, suspending PT/OT sessions.

New patient intake at Hope Valley for rehab following amputation and neuroma surgery; pain 4/10 currently (range 2-9), on Gabapentin 600mg TID and Tylenol Extra Strength, off work, poor sleep due to phantom sensations.

Physical therapy initial evaluation at Hope Valley for status post left transhumeral amputation with phantom limb pain and neuroma revision; left shoulder abduction 120/180, flexion 130/180, pain 5/10; plan for therapy 2-3x weekly for 12-18 months.

Delivery and initial fitting of custom myoelectric left transhumeral prosthesis (carbon-fiber socket, Utah Myoelectric Elbow, Motion Control MC Hand) by CPO Robert Chen; 80% accuracy in electrode signal control demonstrated.
PT visit 1 at Hope Valley: electrode placement practice and signal control exercises, pain 5/10.
PT visit 2 at Hope Valley: object grasp drills, shoulder fatigue noted at 15 minutes, pain 4/10.
PT visit 3 at Hope Valley: repetitive grasping of cups, increasing prosthesis wearing time to 2 hours, pain 4/10.
PT visit 4 at Hope Valley: bilateral upper extremity coordination tasks, pain 3/10.
Patient no-showed scheduled Hope Valley PT appointment; voicemail left, reschedule offered.
PT visit 5 at Hope Valley: prosthetic hand orientation drills, cooking simulator tasks, pain 3/10.
PT visit 6 at Hope Valley: resisted shoulder exercises, left side core stabilization, pain 2/10; patient attributed missed visits to holiday workload and transportation issues.
PT visit 7 at Hope Valley: heavy carrying simulation, industrial tool adaptation, pain 2/10.
Patient no-showed scheduled Hope Valley PT appointment; voicemail left, reschedule offered.
PT visit 8 at Hope Valley: simulating maintenance task actions, push-pull mechanics, pain 1/10.
PT visit 9 at Hope Valley: fine motor control practice manipulating screws and small bolts, pain 1/10.
PT visit 10 at Hope Valley: final functional capacity evaluation with prosthetic arm, pain 1/10.

Physical therapy discharge summary: patient achieved master-level operation of myoelectric prosthesis, independent ADLs, driving, and carrying up to 25 lbs; near-normal left shoulder ROM; discharged to return to modified light/medium duty at NSK.
